extracted.intended_audience: writers, orators, and literary critics interested in producing or evaluating sublime style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and judging the 'Sublime' in poetry and oratory: what it is, its sources, how art and practice can cultivate it, and the vices that destroy it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Sublime ... consists in a certain loftiness and excellence of language” that “takes the reader out of himself” and “acts with an imperious and irresistible force, sways every reader whether he will or no.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sublime passage does not merely persuade the reason but elevates and transports the reader; it is a quality of language that produces an immediate, overpowering effect. Evaluate passages by whether they produce this uplift rather than merely logical persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teachability — role of art vs. genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Sublime originates in nature and genius, art and disciplined practice can aid and regulate it: “a writer can only learn from art when he is to abandon himself to the direction of his genius.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art supplies precision, timing, and control without killing inspiration. Evaluate process by whether craft refines and channels genius (e.g., selection, timing, restraint) rather than smothering it with formulaic devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandeur of Thought (one source of the Sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grandeur of thought arises from nobility of soul and from selecting the most striking circumstances; it includes amplification, imitation of great models, and vivid imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether ideas are elevated and large in scope, spring from a noble temperament, and whether the writer chooses striking facts or incidents. Look for amplification that clarifies and magnifies, imitation of exemplars used as ideals (not slavish copying), and powerful imagery that embodies great thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of moving the Passions (one source of the Sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to affect the reader emotionally — to move the passions — is identified as a central source of sublimity (treated by Longinus as closely tied to oratory and pathos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether writing genuinely engages and moves readers' emotions in ways appropriate to the subject, avoiding empty or ill-timed displays. (Longinus treats this at length in a related discussion of the pathetic.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures of Speech (one source of the Sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rhetorical figures contribute to sublimity: adjuration, rhetorical question, asyndeton, hyperbaton, changes of number/person/tense, periphrasis, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess skillful and strategic use of figures: e.g., adjuration can intensify appeal; rhetorical questions can heighten involvement; asyndeton can quicken pace; hyperbaton can emphasize. The figures should be used to intensify meaning, not to call attention to themselves. Evaluate both appropriateness and concealment of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graceful Expression / Choice of Words (one source of the Sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of appropriate, striking words and tasteful ornaments of style (including metaphors and similes) produces grace and contributes to the Sublime: “the marvellous power and enthralling charm of appropriate and striking words.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate diction for aptness, freshness, and resonance; metaphors should be accumulated judiciously and not abused into tasteless conceits. Familiar words can be used effectively but require care; the goal is expressive precision and aesthetic force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity and Elevation of Structure (one source of the Sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall structure, including modulation of syllables and composition (sentence and paragraph architecture), contributes to sublimity by producing dignity and elevation of effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess larger organizational features: rhythmic modulation, cadence, sentence length and balance, and higher-level composition that yields a majestic whole. Structure should support the loftiness of thought and not be merely ornamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art to conceal Art (technique of sublimity)
rubrics_metrics.description: True art conceals itself: rhetorical art should not be ostentatious but should hide the means so that the effect seems natural and spontaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether rhetorical devices are seamlessly integrated. Devices that call attention to themselves undermine sublimity; mastery shows when craft is invisible and the reader feels only the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and Amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful selection of the most striking circumstances and judicious amplification (expanding and intensifying a point) are means to reach sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the writer has chosen the most illustrative and elevated material and whether amplification clarifies and heightens rather than bloats or digresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation of Great Models (emulation, not slavish copying)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use past masters (Homer, Demosthenes, etc.) as beacons and judges of one's work—emulate their greatness to inspire one’s own, but avoid mechanical imitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the writer learns standards and sensibilities from exemplars and then produces original greatness. Ask: Would the great masters approve? Use posterity and past masters as corrective standards during revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and Abuse of Metaphor (ornaments of style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphors can enrich style when accumulated and apt; abused metaphors and tasteless conceits produce frigidity or ridicule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess quality, freshness, and appropriateness of metaphors. Beware of piling metaphors without connective purpose or using far-fetched conceits that distract. Good metaphors illuminate; bad ones obfuscate or amuse unintentionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of Tone and Emotion (avoid false sentiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'false sentiment'—empty or ill-timed displays of emotion that have no connection to the subject, or emotion disproportionate to the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate authenticity and fit of emotional expression. Emotional passages should arise naturally from subject and situation; gratuitous or inflated feeling undermines credibility and fails to move readers truly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Bombast (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bombast (pretentious, inflated language) 'transcends the Sublime' and becomes ludicrous; it is a common pitfall for those attempting loftiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag grandiloquence that rings false: overwritten, tautological, or hyperbolic phrasing that aims at loftiness but collapses into absurdity. Effective evaluation rejects bulk without substance and favors genuine elevation over mere pomp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Puerility / Frigidity / Affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Puerility (pedantic over-elaboration), frigidity, and affectation are vices opposed to sublimity; they produce paltriness and silly ornamentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for pedantic niceties, forced cleverness, or over-polished glitter that drain passion and nobility. Good style avoids seeking attractiveness at the cost of power and substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Abuse of Rhythm and Cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythmic abuse—misuse of cadence or awkward modulation of syllables—can destroy sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether rhythm supports meaning; monitor for artificial or monotonous cadences, jerky clauses, or forced prosody that distracts rather than elevates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Broken and Jerky Clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Disjointed, broken-sentence construction interferes with lofty effect and can make prose seem undignified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clauses that interrupt flow or create incoherence. Smooth but varied sentence construction aids elevation; staccato fragmentation should be used sparingly and purposefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Undue Prolixity (excessive wordiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlong, prolix expression undermines the Sublime by diluting force and tiring the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate concision: whether verbosity serves amplification or merely pads. Powerful sublimity often relies on well-timed brevity as much as on expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard Against Improper Use of Familiar Words and Anti-climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Misusing commonplace words or committing anti-climax (falling from high to petty) damages sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess diction transitions and climactic arcs. Avoid dropping to trivial language or ideas after a high passage; ensure continuity of tone and appropriateness of vocabulary throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Acceptance as an External Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Longinus suggests the external canon of sublimity is broad acceptance: 'will always please, and please all readers'—the verdict not of a narrow coterie but of the large public and posterity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both popular and lasting judgment as a corrective: does the passage have the qualities that make it likely to stand the test of time and wide readership? That said, allow for the role of elite exemplars in shaping standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and Psychological Foundation (nobility of soul)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dignity and fire of style derive from dignity and fire of soul; moral greatness in the author underpins sublime expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the writer's convictions, moral seriousness, and inner grandeur are evident in the text. Sublimity is not merely technical but reflects character and seriousness of purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Revision Discipline — write for posterity and the masters
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical counsel: revise by asking 'How would Homer/Demosthenes/other great ones judge this?' and 'How will posterity read this?' Use these standards to prune fads and trivial cleverness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess revision practices: does the writer excise momentary cleverness and test passages against durable exemplars? This discipline is recommended as a method to approach sublimity.
